name: NJ-06
label: Safe D

key_factors: Longtime incumbent Frank Pallone running in a D+5 district
Massive financial advantage: $3.1M cash vs. under $2,000 for the challenger
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~95%
No polling or expert ratings, but fundamentals strongly favor Democrats
model.rationale: The baseline model's 19-point margin aligns with the district's lean, incumbency, and a lopsided money gap; the Republican challenger has raised only $7,645 and has essentially no resources. Prediction markets at 95% for Democrats corroborate a Safe D rating.
model.watch: A late surge of outside spending against Pallone or an unusually strong national Republican environment could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Frank Pallone, a longtime Democratic incumbent, is running for reelection in a New Jersey district with a modest Democratic lean of about five points. The fundamentals strongly favor him: incumbency, a favorable national environment for the party in this baseline, and an overwhelming financial advantage of more than $3 million on hand against a challenger who has raised under $8,000.

There are no public polls or expert ratings for this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals and prediction markets, which put the Democratic win probability around 95 percent. With the challenger lacking any visible campaign infrastructure, this race is rated Safe Democratic, with the expected margin near 19 points.
